5.h: 1 - Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Allāh * (م، ق) .
5.t:
Ibn al-Jarrāḥ ibn Hilāl ibn Uhayb ibn Ḍabbah ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Fihr ibn Mālik ibn al-Naḍr ibn Kinānah ibn Khuzaymah ibn Mudrikah ibn Ilyās ibn Muḍar ibn Nizār ibn Maʿadd ibn ʿAdnān al-Qurashī, al-Fihrī, al-Makkī.
One of the first forerunners, and one whom al-Ṣiddīq resolved to appoint to the caliphate (الخلافة), and whom he put forward on the day of ⟦1:5⟧ al-Saqīfah, owing to his complete fitness in the view of Abū Bakr (1) .
He and the Prophet ﷺ meet in lineage at Fihr.
The Prophet ﷺ bore witness that he would enter Paradise, and named him: the Trustee of the Community; his virtues are famous and numerous.
He narrated a limited number of hadiths (2) , and took part in notable campaigns.
Narrating from him: العرباض بن سارية، وجابر بن عبد الله، وأبو أمامة الباهلي، وسمرة بن جندب، وأسلم مولى عمر، وعبد الرحمن بن غنم، وآخرون.
He has one hadith in (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim) , one hadith in (Jāmiʿ Abī ʿĪsā) , and in (Musnad Baqī) he has fifteen hadiths.
Narration from him:
أخبرنا أبو المعالي محمد بن عبد السلام التميمي، قراءة عليه في سنة أربع وتسعين وست مائة، أنبأنا أبو روح عبد المعز بن محمد البزاز، أنبأنا تميم بن أبي سعيد أبو القاسم المعري، في رجب سنة تسع وعشرين وخمس مائة بهراة، أنبأنا أبو سعد محمد بن عبد الرحمن، أنبأنا أبو عمرو بن حمدان، أخبرنا أبو يعلى أحمد بن علي، حدثنا عبد الله بن معاوية القرشي، حدثنا حماد بن سلمة، عن خالد الحذاء، عن عبد الله بن شقيق، عن (3) عبد الله بن سراقة، عن أبي عبيدة بن الجراح: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saying: (There was no ⟦1:6⟧ prophet after Noah but he warned his people of the Dajjāl, and I am warning you of him) .
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ described him to us and said: (Perhaps some of those who have seen me, or heard my speech, will live to see him) .
They said: O Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless you and grant you peace! How will our hearts be on that day? Like they are today?
He said: (Or better (1)) .
Al-Tirmidhī recorded it, from ʿAbd Allāh al-Jumaḥī, so we have matched him with an elevated chain (العالي).
He said: on this topic there are also reports from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Busr and others.
This is a sound (الحسن), gharīb (الغريب) hadith from the hadith of Abū ʿUbaydah (may Allah be pleased with him).
Ibn Saʿd said in (al-Ṭabaqāt) : أخبرنا محمد بن عمر، حدثني ثور بن يزيد، عن خالد بن معدان، عن مالك بن يخامر:
That he described Abū ʿUbaydah, and said: He was a lean man, gaunt of face, thin of beard, tall, stooping (2) , gap-toothed (3) in the two front incisors (4) .
وأخبرنا محمد بن عمر، حدثنا محمد بن صالح، عن يزيد بن رومان، قال: Ibn Maẓʿūn, ʿUbaydah ibn al-Ḥārith, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, Abū Salamah ⟦1:7⟧ ibn ʿAbd al-Asad, and Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ set out until they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he presented Islam to them and told them of its laws, and they became Muslim at the same moment; that was before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the house of al-Arqam.
Abū ʿUbaydah was present at Badr, and on that day he killed his father; he fought valiantly on the day of Uḥud, and on that day he pulled out the two rings of the helmet that had entered the cheek of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from a blow that struck him, and his own two front teeth came out, yet his mouth looked better for their loss, so that it was said: no one with missing front teeth was ever seen more handsome than Abū ʿUbaydah with his missing front teeth (1) .
Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq said, at the time of the death of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, at the Saqīfah of Banū Sāʿidah:
I am content for you with one of these two men: ʿUmar, or Abū ʿUbaydah.
Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār said: the line of Abū ʿUbaydah has died out, as have the offspring of all his brothers; and he was among those who emigrated to the land of Abyssinia.
Ibn Isḥāq and al-Wāqidī said this (2) .
I say: if he did emigrate there, his stay there (3) was not long.
Abū ʿUbaydah was counted among those who collected the Mighty Qurʾān.
Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah said in his (Maghāzī) : the campaign of ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ is the campaign of Dhāt al-Salāsil (4) , on the borderlands of Syria; ʿAmr feared for that flank of his, so he sought reinforcement from the Messenger ⟦1:8⟧ of Allah ﷺ, who called upon Abū Bakr and ʿUmar among a band of the notables of the Muhājirūn, and the Prophet of Allah placed Abū ʿUbaydah in command over them.
When they came to ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, he said: I am your commander.
The Muhājirūn said: Rather, you are the commander of your companions, and our commander is Abū ʿUbaydah.
ʿAmr said: You are only reinforcements sent to support me.
When Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ saw that — and he was a man of good character, gentle of temperament, a follower of the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his instruction — he handed over the command to ʿAmr.
It is established through several routes from Anas:
That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Every community has a trustee, and the trustee of this community is: Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ (1)) .
أخبرنا عبد الرحمن بن محمد الفقيه، وغيره إجازة، قالوا:
أخبرنا حنبل بن عبد الله، أنبأنا هبة الله بن محمد، أنبأنا أبو علي بن المذهب، أخبرنا أبو بكر القطيعي، حدثنا عبد الله بن أحمد، حدثني أبي، حدثنا أبو المغيرة، حدثنا صفوان، عن شريح بن عبيد، وراشد بن سعد، وغيرهما، قالوا:
When ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb reached Sargh (2) , he was told that there was a severe plague in Syria, and he said: If my appointed time ⟦1:9⟧ comes to me while Abū ʿUbaydah is alive, I will appoint him as my successor; and if Allah, Mighty and Majestic, asks me: Why did you appoint him over the community of Muḥammad?
I say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: (Every community has a trustee, and the trustee of this community is: Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ) .
He said: The people disapproved of that, and said: What of the nobles of Quraysh?
They meant: Banū Fihr.
Then he said: And if my appointed time comes to me when Abū ʿUbaydah has died, I will appoint Muʿādh ibn Jabal as successor; and if my Lord asks me, I say:
I heard Your Prophet say: (He will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection ahead of the scholars by a stone’s throw (1)) .
وروى: حماد بن سلمة، عن الجريري، عن عبد الله بن شقيق، عن عمرو بن العاص، قال:
It was said: O Messenger of Allah! Which of the people is dearest to you?
He said: (ʿĀʾishah) .
It was said: Among the men?
He said: (Abū Bakr) .
It was said: Then who?
He said: (Then Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ) .
This is how Ḥammād narrates it.
A group contradicted him, and narrated it: عن الجريري، عن عبد الله، قال:
I asked ʿĀʾishah: Which of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was dearest to him?
She said: Abū Bakr, then ʿUmar, then Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ (2) . ⟦1:10⟧
أخبرنا إسماعيل بن عبد الرحمن المعدل، أنبأنا عبد الله بن أحمد الفقيه، أنبأنا محمد بن عبد الباقي، أنبأنا أبو الفضل بن خيرون، أنبأنا أحمد بن محمد بن غالب، بقراءته (1) على أبي العباس بن حمدان، حدثكم محمد بن أيوب، أنبأنا أبو الوليد، أنبأنا شعبة، عن أبي إسحاق، سمعت صلة بن زفر (2) ، عن حذيفة:
That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (I shall send to you a trustworthy man) .
The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked eagerly towards it, and he sent Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ (3) .
Both agreed upon (المتفق عليه) it from the hadith of Shuʿbah.
And both agreed upon (المتفق عليه) it: من حديث خالد الحذاء، عن أبي قلابة، عن أنس:
That the Prophet ﷺ said: (Every community has a trustee, and the trustee of this community is: Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ (4)) .
أخبرنا أحمد بن محمد المعلم، أنبأنا أبو القاسم بن رواحة، أنبأنا أبو طاهر الحافظ، أنبأنا أحمد بن علي الصوفي، وأبو غالب الباقلاني، وجماعة، قالوا:
أنبأنا أبو القاسم بن بشران، أنبأنا أبو محمد الفاكهي بمكة، حدثنا أبو يحيى بن أبي ميسرة، حدثنا عبد الوهاب بن عيسى الواسطي، أنبأنا يحيى بن أبي زكريا، حدثنا عبد الله بن عثمان بن خثيم، عن أبي الزبير، عن جابر، قال: I was ⟦1:11⟧ in the army that was with Khālid, with whom he reinforced Abū ʿUbaydah while he was besieging Damascus; when we came to them, he said to Khālid: Go forward and lead the prayer, for you are more entitled to lead it, since you came to reinforce me.
Khālid said: I would not go ahead of a man of whom I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: (Every community has a trustee, and the trustee of this community is: Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ (1)) .
Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah: أنبأنا عبد الرحيم بن سليمان، عن زكريا بن (2) أبي زائدة، عن أبي إسحاق، عن صلة، عن حذيفة، قال:
The two bishops of Najrān, al-ʿĀqib and al-Sayyid, came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: Send with us a trustworthy man, truly trustworthy.
He said: (I shall send with you a trustworthy man, truly trustworthy) .
The people looked eagerly towards it, and he said: (Stand up, O Abū ʿUbaydah) .
And he sent him with them.
He said: وحدثنا وكيع، عن سفيان، عن أبي إسحاق،  something similar (3) .
Al-Turqufī (4) in his (Juzʾ) : حدثنا أبو المغيرة، حدثنا صفوان بن عمرو، حدثنا أبو حسبة (5) مسلم بن أكيس مولى ابن كريز، عن أبي عبيدة، قال: someone who ⟦1:12⟧ went in to him mentioned to me that he found him weeping, and said: What makes you weep, O Abū ʿUbaydah?
He said: What makes me weep is that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one day mentioned what Allah would open up for the Muslims, until he mentioned Syria, and said: (If Allah prolongs your life, then three servants are enough for you: a servant to serve you, a servant to travel with you, and a servant to serve your family; and three mounts are enough for you: a mount for your riding, a mount for your baggage, and a mount for your servant boy) .
Yet here I am, looking at my house filled with slaves, and at my stable filled with horses; so how shall I meet the Messenger of Allah ﷺ after this? He enjoined us: (The dearest of you to me, and the closest of you to me, is the one who meets me in the same state in which I left you (1)) .
A gharīb (الغريب) hadith.
Aḥmad also narrated it in his (Musnad) , from Abū al-Mughīrah.
Wakīʿ ibn al-Jarrāḥ: مبارك بن فضالة، عن الحسن:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (There is none of you but, if I wished, I could find fault with some of his character, except Abū ʿUbaydah) .
This is mursal (مرسل) (2) .
Abū ʿUbaydah was described as having good character, abundant forbearance, and humility.
Muḥammad ibn Saʿd said: حدثنا أحمد بن عبد الله، حدثنا ابن عيينة، عن ابن ⟦1:13⟧ أبي نجيح: ʿUmar said to those sitting with him: Make wishes.
So they made wishes, and ʿUmar said: But I wish for a house filled with men like Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ (1) .
Ibn Abī Shaybah said: قال ابن أبي شيبة: قال ابن (2) علية، عن يونس، عن الحسن:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (There is none of my Companions but, if I wished, I could find fault with him, except Abū ʿUbaydah (3)) .
And Sufyān al-Thawrī: عن أبي إسحاق، عن أبي عبيدة، قال:
Ibn Masʿūd said: My close friends among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ are three: Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and Abū ʿUbaydah (4) .
Others contradicted him, for in (al-Jaʿdiyyāt) : أنبأنا زهير، عن أبي إسحاق، عن أبي ⟦1:14⟧
الأحوص، عن عبد الله ... , and he mentioned it (1) .
Khalīfah ibn Khayyāṭ said: Abū Bakr had put Abū ʿUbaydah in charge of the treasury (2) .
I say: he means the property of the Muslims, for no treasury had yet been established; the first to set one up was ʿUmar.
Khalīfah said: Then Abū Bakr sent him to Syria in the year 13 AH as a commander; in that year ʿUmar became caliph, dismissed Khālid ibn al-Walīd, and appointed Abū ʿUbaydah (3) .
Al-Qāsim ibn Yazīd said: حدثنا سفيان، عن زياد بن فياض، عن تميم بن سلمة:
That ʿUmar met Abū ʿUbaydah, shook his hand and kissed his hand, and the two withdrew aside weeping (4) .
Ibn al-Mubārak said in his (al-Jihād) : عن هشام بن سعد، عن زيد بن أسلم، عن أبيه، قال:
It reached ʿUmar that Abū ʿUbaydah was besieged in Syria and that the enemy had inflicted harm on him, so ʿUmar wrote to him: To proceed: no hardship befalls a believing servant but Allah makes relief after it, and one hardship will not overcome two eases: “O you who have believed, be patient, vie in patience, and stand on guard” , the verse [Qurʾān 3:200] .
He said: Abū ʿUbaydah wrote back to him:
To proceed: Allah says: “Know that the life of this world is but play and amusement” , up to His words: “the enjoyment of delusion” [Qurʾān 57:20] .
He said: ʿUmar went out ⟦1:15⟧ with his letter, read it on the pulpit, and said:
O people of Medina! Abū ʿUbaydah is only alluding to you, or to me; be eager for jihad (1) .
Ibn Abī Fudayk: عن هشام بن سعد، عن زيد، عن أبيه، قال:
It reached me that Muʿādh heard a man say: If Khālid ibn al-Walīd were here, the people would not be in turmoil (2) .
That was during the siege of Abū ʿUbaydah, and Muʿādh said: Is it to Abū ʿUbaydah, then, that incapacity is to be imputed, you fatherless man! By Allah, he is the best of those who remain on the earth.
Al-Bukhārī narrated it in his (Tārīkh) , and Ibn Saʿd (3) .
And in (al-Zuhd) by Ibn al-Mubārak: حدثنا معمر، عن هشام بن عروة، عن أبيه، قال:
ʿUmar came to Syria, and the commanders and notables went out to meet him.
He said: Where is my brother Abū ʿUbaydah?
They said: He is coming to you now.
He said: He came on a she-camel haltered with a rope, greeted him, then said to the people: Leave us.
He went along with him until he reached his lodging, and stayed with him, and he saw nothing in his house but his sword, his shield and his saddle.
ʿUmar said to him: If only you had acquired some furnishings — or he said: something.
He said: O ⟦1:16⟧ Commander of the Faithful (أمير المؤمنين)! This will suffice to bring us to our resting place (1) .
Ibn Wahb: حدثني عبد الله بن عمر، عن نافع، عن ابن عمر:
That ʿUmar, when he came to Syria, said to Abū ʿUbaydah: Take us to your lodging.
He said: And what will you do at my place? You only want to wring tears from your eyes over me.
He said: So he went in and saw nothing; he said: Where are your furnishings? I see only a felt mat, a bowl (2) and a water-skin, and you are a commander! Do you have any food?
Abū ʿUbaydah got up and went to a small basket, and took some broken pieces of bread from it, and ʿUmar wept; Abū ʿUbaydah said to him: I told you that you would wring tears from your eyes over me, O Commander of the Faithful (أمير المؤمنين); what brings you to your resting place is enough for you.
ʿUmar said: This world has changed all of us except you, O Abū ʿUbaydah (3) .
Abū Dāwūd recorded it in his (Sunan) , by way of Ibn al-Aʿrābī.
This -by Allah- is true asceticism, not the asceticism of one who was poor and destitute.
Maʿn ibn ʿĪsā, from Mālik:
That ʿUmar sent Abū ʿUbaydah four thousand, or four hundred dinars, and said to the messenger: See what he does with it.
He said: Abū ʿUbaydah distributed it; then he sent the like of it to Muʿādh.
He said: He distributed it, except for something of which his wife told him: we need it; when the messenger informed ʿUmar, he said: Praise be to Allah, who has placed in Islam those who do ⟦1:17⟧ this (1) .
Al-Fasawī (2) : حدثنا أبو اليمان، عن جرير بن عثمان، عن أبي الحسن عمران بن نمران:
That Abū ʿUbaydah used to go about the army camp, saying: Lo, many a one who whitens his clothes defiles his religion! Lo, many a one who honours himself is in fact debasing it! Outstrip the old evil deeds with new good deeds (3) .
Thābit al-Bunānī said: Abū ʿUbaydah said:
O people! I am a man of Quraysh, and there is none among you, red or black, who surpasses me in piety but I would wish that I were in his skin (4) .
Maʿmar, from Qatādah: Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ said:
I wish I were a ram, that my family would slaughter me, eat my flesh, and sip my broth (5) .
ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn said: I wish I were ashes scattered by the wind (6) .
Shuʿbah: عن قيس بن مسلم، عن طارق:
That ʿUmar wrote to Abū ʿUbaydah during the plague: A need has arisen for me in which I cannot do without you, so hasten to me.
When he read the letter, he said: I know the need of the Commander of the Faithful (أمير المؤمنين); he wants to preserve one who is not going to remain.
So he wrote: I know your need, so release me from your firm command, for I am in an army ⟦1:18⟧ among the armies of the Muslims, and I do not wish to keep myself apart from them.
When ʿUmar read the letter, he wept, and it was said to him: Has Abū ʿUbaydah died?
He said: No, but it is as though he has (1) .
He said: Then Abū ʿUbaydah died, and the plague lifted.
Abū al-Muwajjih Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr al-Marwazī said: They claimed that Abū ʿUbaydah was with 36,000 troops, and only 6,000 men of them remained.
أخبرنا محمد بن عبد السلام، عن أبي روح، أنبأنا أبو سعد، أنبأنا ابن (2) حمدان، أنبأنا أبو يعلى، حدثنا عبد الله بن محمد بن أسماء، حدثنا مهدي بن ميمون، حدثنا واصل مولى أبي (3) عيينة، عن ابن (4) أبي سيف المخزومي، عن الوليد بن عبد الرحمن -شامي، فقيه- عن عياض بن غطيف، قال:
I visited Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ in his illness, and his wife Tuḥayfah was sitting at his head, while he had his face turned toward the wall; I said: How did Abū ʿUbaydah spend the night?
She said: He spent the night earning reward.
He said: I -by Allah- did not spend the night earning reward!
It was as if that troubled the people, so he said: Will you not ask me about what I said?
They said: We did not like what you said, so how should we ask you?
He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: (Whoever spends an outlay over and above in the path of Allah, it is seven hundredfold; and whoever spends on his dependants, or visits a sick person, or removes something harmful, then the good deed is worth ten like it; fasting ⟦1:19⟧ is a shield as long as one does not tear it (1) ; and whomever Allah afflicts with an affliction in his body, it is an expiation for him (2)) .
أنبأنا جماعة، قالوا:
أنبأنا ابن طبرزد، أنبأنا ابن الحصين، أنبأنا ابن غيلان، أنبأنا أبو بكر الشافعي، أنبأنا عبد الله بن أحمد، حدثنا محمد بن أبان الواسطي، حدثني جرير بن حازم، حدثني بشار بن أبي سيف، حدثني الوليد بن عبد الرحمن، عن عياض بن غطيف، قال:
Abū ʿUbaydah fell ill, and we went in to visit him, and he said:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: (Fasting is a shield as long as one does not tear it (3)) .
The Prophet ﷺ appointed Abū ʿUbaydah more than once, among them the time in which his troops went hungry — they were three hundred — and the sea cast up for them the whale called al-ʿAnbar.
Abū ʿUbaydah said: Carrion.
Then he said: No; we are the envoys of the Messenger of Allah, and in the path of Allah, so eat ... , and he mentioned the hadith.
It is in the two Ṣaḥīḥs (الصحيحين) (4) . ⟦1:20⟧
When al-Ṣiddīq had finished with the war against the people of the Apostasy and the war against Musaylimah the Liar, he equipped the commanders (1) of the armies for the conquest of Syria.
He sent Abū ʿUbaydah, Yazīd ibn Abī Sufyān, ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ and Shuraḥbīl ibn Ḥasanah; the battle of Ajnādayn (2) took place near al-Ramlah, and Allah granted victory to the believers, and the good news came while al-Ṣiddīq was in his final illness; then came the battle of Faḥl (3) and the battle of Marj al-Ṣuffar (4) ; Abū Bakr had dispatched Khālid to campaign in Iraq, then sent to him to come to the aid of those in Syria.
So he crossed the wastes of the desert of al-Samāwah, and al-Ṣiddīq gave him command over all the commanders; they besieged Damascus, and Abū Bakr died.
ʿUmar hastened to dismiss Khālid, and appointed Abū ʿUbaydah over all of them; the letter of appointment came to him, but he kept it secret for a while — all of this from his religiousness, his gentleness and his forbearance — and the conquest of Damascus (5) was at his hands; at that point he made the appointment public, in order to conclude ⟦1:21⟧ the peace treaty with the Byzantines; they opened the gate of al-Jābiyah to him by treaty, and lo, Khālid had taken the city by force from the Eastern Gate, and Abū ʿUbaydah upheld the treaty for them.
From al-Mughīrah: that Abū ʿUbaydah made peace with them on the basis of half of their churches and dwellings; then Abū ʿUbaydah was the head of Islam on the day of the battle of al-Yarmūk, in which Allah uprooted the armies of the Byzantines, and a great multitude of them were killed.
Ibn al-Mubārak narrated in his (al-Zuhd) ; he said:
أنبأنا عبد الحميد بن بهرام، عن شهر بن حوشب، قال:
حدثني عبد الرحمن بن غنم، عن حديث الحارث بن عميرة، قال:
Muʿādh ibn Jabal took me by the hand, and sent him to Abū ʿUbaydah, and he asked him: How is he! — when the two of them had been struck by the plague?
Abū ʿUbaydah showed him a plague sore that had come out on his palm, and its gravity weighed heavily on al-Ḥārith’s mind, and he was frightened of it when he saw it; and Abū ʿUbaydah swore by Allah that he would not love to have red camels in its place (1) .
وعن الأسود، عن عروة: That Abū ʿUbaydah and his family had been spared the illness of ʿAmwās, and he said: O Allah, Your share in the family of Abū ʿUbaydah!
He said: Then a pustule came out on Abū ʿUbaydah, on his little finger, and he began looking at it; it was said to him: It is nothing.
He said: I hope that Allah will put blessing in it, for when He blesses something small, it becomes much (2) .
Al-Walīd ibn Muslim: حدثني أبو بكر بن أبي مريم، عن صالح بن أبي المخارق، قال:
Abū ʿUbaydah set out from al-Jābiyah to Jerusalem for prayer, ⟦1:22⟧ and appointed Muʿādh ibn Jabal as his deputy over the people (1) .
Al-Walīd said: Someone who heard ʿUrwah ibn Ruwaym narrated to me; he said:
His appointed time overtook him at Faḥl, and he died there, near Baysān (2) .
The plague of ʿAmwās: named after the village of ʿAmwās, which lies between al-Ramlah and Jerusalem.
As for al-Aṣmaʿī, he said (3) : it comes from their saying at the time of the plague: ʿamma wa-āsā (it spread and it brought grief).
Abū Ḥafṣ al-Fallās said: Abū ʿUbaydah died in the year 18 AH, aged 58; he used to dye with henna and katam (4) , and he had two braids.
A group said the same regarding his death.
Ibn ʿĀʾidh was alone in reporting, from Abū Mushir, that he read in the book of Yazīd ibn ʿUbaydah: that Abū ʿUbaydah died in the year 17 AH.
